title: Example 286 protected-state tasks at the frozen bound through the bean wrapper's stand-ins, again: the refutation on 5.3.18, and where the fixed task stops
description: The state stream of the domain-advances brief, steps 2 and 3. A rerun of job 20261117-181750, which failed before the check ran: with a relative --work, the observer of PropertyEditorRegistrySupport's initializer was given a relative -Xlog file while its JVM ran in the observed/ folder, so the JVM refused the option. lib/src/observed.rs now makes that folder absolute; the test an_observed_initializer_is_observed_with_a_relative_work_folder (lib/tests/claims.rs) runs the CLI from another directory with a relative --work and failed the same way before the fix. The frozen claim examples/286-spring-framework-cve-2022-22968-case-sensitive-disallowed-fields/claims/protected-age-not-mutated.json, unchanged (DataBinder.bind of one property value named field with the value "32" onto a fresh ProtectedBean, age protected by one disallowed pattern, leaves age 0, for every simple name of at most 8 units), run by examples/286-spring-framework-cve-2022-22968-case-sensitive-disallowed-fields/proofs/prove.py at its own bound 8 (unwind 16, strict gaps; the ArrayList, ArrayDeque, HashSet and PropertyChangeEvent models; PropertyEditorRegistrySupport and ClassUtils observed; the stand-ins ProtectedBeanStandIn for the bean wrapper's write of a property value and ProtectedBeanTypeStandIn for a property's type, each sampled against the release on a JVM before the run). A capped probe of the vulnerable task at bound 8 refuted it in 63 s at ageAfterBinding(false, "Age"), which returns 32 on a JVM, so the refutation rests on no stand-in or model; a probe at bound 3 with a relative --work refutes it again after the fix. This job's outcome and evidence.json are what examples/tools/accept.py reads to accept it. The fixed task is expected to stop with no verdict at String.toLowerCase() on a non-ASCII field (DataBinder.isAllowed:828: the frozen claim does not restrict field to ASCII, and the checker lowers ASCII only), which this job records as the current blocker. 2 CPUs: the JVMs the observer and the stand-ins' samplers start need two.
expected: the vulnerable step exits 0 with 'verdict: violation (expected violation)' at the claim's bound 8 with a witness run on a JVM (field="Age" or another case variant that binds age); the fixed step exits 1 with 'verdict: unverifiable' naming the gap java.lang.String.toLowerCase() at DataBinder.isAllowed:828, and any other gap is a finding to record

resources.notes: the inline probe of the vulnerable step at bound 8 took 63 s in under 4 GB, the lemma's proof included; the fixed step stops at its gap within minutes; each stand-in sampler runs a few seconds
